rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī warns that prolonged historical and literary debate about Abraham can obscure the Qur’an’s interpretive aim; the story first presents his confrontation with the man called Azar.
rows.anchor: وقد أطالوا هذا النمط من البحث حتى انجر إلى غايات بعيدة تغيب عندها رسوم البحث التفسيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an presents Abraham first opposing the man it calls his father Azar over idols, insisting on monotheism until Azar expelled him and ordered him away.
rows.anchor: بدأ بشأن رجل يذكر القرآن أنه كان أباه آزر، وقد أصر عليه أن يرفض الأصنام ويتبعه في دين التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham answered Azar with peace and promised to seek forgiveness, perhaps hoping to draw him toward faith and its happiness and guidance.
rows.anchor: فسلم عليه إبراهيم ووعده أن يستغفر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context indicates Abraham promised to pray for Azar during worldly life, not to intercede for him at resurrection while he remained an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: والآية الثانية أحسن قرينة على أنه عليه السلام إنما وعده أن يستغفر له في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asking forgiveness for his misguided father followed death or separation, as shown by was misguided; its wording appears to fulfill his promise while describing the Hereafter where only a sound heart helps.
rows.anchor: وقوله { إنه كان من الضالين } يدل على أنه عليه السلام إنما دعا بهذا الدعاء لأبيه بعد موته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context of the general prohibition on seeking forgiveness for idolaters shows that Abraham’s prayer for his father and later disavowal both occurred in worldly life; the exception was fulfillment of a promise.
rows.anchor: والآية بسياقها تشهد على أن هذا الدعاء إنما صدر منه عليه السلام في الدنيا وكذلك التبري منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an explains that Abraham’s promised prayer was an exception to his disavowal of his people, and that he disavowed Azar when Azar proved God’s enemy.
rows.anchor: وما كان استغفار إبراهيم لأبيه الا عن موعدة وعدها إياه فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer and disavowal belong to Abraham’s early period before migration, when he sought judgment, the company of the righteous, and offspring, then went to the blessed land and received Isaac and Jacob.
rows.anchor: وكل ذلك في أوائل عهد إبراهيم ولما يهاجر إلى الأرض المقدسة بدليل سؤاله الحق واللحوق بالصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s final recorded prayer for his parents belongs to his late Meccan period, after migration, the settling of Ishmael, the city’s growth, and the Kaaba’s construction.
rows.anchor: ثم يذكر تعالى آخر دعائه بمكة وقد وقع في آخر عهده عليه السلام بعد ما هاجر إلى الأرض المقدسة وولد له الأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parent Abraham includes in his final prayer is not Azar: he had already prayed for Azar in fulfillment of a promise and disavowed him as God’s enemy.
rows.anchor: والآية بما لها من السياق وبما احتف بها من القرائن أحسن شاهد على أن والده الذي دعا له فيها غير الذي يذكره سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī concludes Azar was not Abraham’s biological father; the Qur’an’s descriptions allow Azar to be called father by an extended title.
rows.anchor: فقد تحصل أن آزر الذي تذكره الآية ليس أبا لإبراهيم حقيقة وإنما كان معنونا ببعض الأوصاف والعناوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic permits ab for a grandfather, uncle, stepfather, guardian, or respected elder; the Qur’an likewise calls Abraham and Ishmael the fathers of Jacob and Isaac the father of Joseph.
rows.anchor: واللغة تسوغ إطلاق الأب على الجد والعم وزوج أم الإنسان بعد أبيه وكل من يتولى أمور الشخص وكل كبير مطاع

rows.speaker: بعض الباحثين
rows.claim: A reported account of narrative art says storytellers may choose any effective path to their purpose without distinguishing historical truth from error or supplying every essential circumstance.
rows.anchor: أن يختار القاص في قصته كل طريق ممكن موصل إلى غايته ومقصده إيصالا حسنا

rows.speaker: بعض الباحثين
rows.claim: On that account, the Qur’an might use stories circulating among its contemporaries or the People of the Book even when their accuracy is unverified, including imagined stories.
rows.anchor: فمن الجائز أن يأخذ القرآن الكريم في سبيل النيل إلى مقصده وهو الهداية إلى السعادة الإنسانية قصصا دائرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects applying fictional-story conventions to the Qur’an: it claims to be God’s truthful guidance, so its reports, arguments, and route to their aims must be true.
rows.anchor: وهذا خطأ فان ما ذكره من أمر الفن القصصي حق غير أن ذلك غير منطبق على مورد القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A purpose cannot be wholly true if its path contains falsehood; a decisive statement cannot rest on careless explanation, and divine report cannot contain ignorance or error.
rows.anchor: وكيف يكون مقصد من المقاصد حقا على الإطلاق وقد تسرب باطل ما إلى طريقه الذي يدعو إليه المقصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpreter’s proper method is to assume the Qur’an truthful in both its aims and its means; judging its truth against other scriptures or scientific disciplines belongs outside tafsir.
rows.anchor: فهذا هو المسلك الوحيد الذي لا يحل تعديه في استنطاق القرآن الكريم في مضامين آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection on the Qur’an shows that one passage can resolve a difficulty or seeming contradiction in another, so interpreters should use its verses to explain one another.
rows.anchor: القرآن تكفي بعض آياته لدفع المشكلة عن بعضها الآخر ويكشف جزء منه عما اشتبه على بعض الأفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a book of guidance, not a history or storybook; genealogy, dates, places, and other historical details have no religious value unless they serve its purpose.
rows.anchor: والقرآن الكريم كتاب دعوة وهداية لا يتخطى عن صراطه ولو خطوة وليس كتاب تاريخ ولا قصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī plans to gather Abraham’s scattered Qur’anic story and compare it with the Torah and other accounts, inviting fair-minded readers to judge what the Qur’an establishes.
rows.anchor: وسنجمع في ذيل البحث عن آيات القصة جملا من قصة إبراهيم عليه السلام منثورة في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an does not neglect useful knowledge or forbid studying nature, earlier peoples, or social patterns; many verses commend knowledge and reflection.
rows.anchor: والقرآن الكريم مع ذلك لم يهمل الواجب في حق العلوم النافعة، ولم يحرم البحث عن العالم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines a ṣanam as an image made from silver, copper, or wood and worshipped as a means of drawing near to God; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī treats these materials as examples.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات الصنم جثة متخذة من فضة أو نحاس أو خشب كانوا يعبدونها متقربين به إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols could be made from any moldable metal or stone, dough as reported of Banū Ḥanīfa, clay, or a sculpted image; their materials were not limited to the lexicon’s examples.
rows.anchor: وقد روى أن بني حنيفة من اليمامة كانوا قد اتخذوا صنما من أقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols represented abstract or concrete gods, and their worshippers used them to approach those gods and the gods to approach Allah; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls it folly to worship a handmade object.
rows.anchor: وقد كانوا يعبدونها تقربا بها إلى أربابها، وبأربابها إلى الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s question means that his people treated insignificant idols as gods, though a true God must be of immense consequence.
rows.anchor: معناه أتتخذ أصناما لا خطر في أمرها آلهة والإله هو الذي في أمره خطر عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolatrous submission is irrational: a maker possessing knowledge and power bows to a product that lacks both, as Abraham also says idols cannot hear, see, or help.
rows.anchor: وكيف لا يظهر هذا الضلال وهو عبادة وتذلل عبودي من صانع فيه آثار العلم والمقدرة لمصنوعه الذي يفقد العلم والقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s short question summarizes several arguments Abraham made against idols, including their being human-made and lacking the qualities of lordship.
rows.anchor: من الحجاج وإن كان بمنزلة التلخيص لعدة احتجاجات واجه بها ابراهيم عليه السلام أباه وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idol debate came first, while the celestial debate followed and the debate with the king came after Abraham’s opposition to idolatry became public and he broke the idols.
rows.anchor: فقد كان أول ما حاج به في التوحيد هو ما حاج به أباه وقومه في أمر الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative thus links the vision of the heavenly kingdom to Abraham’s preceding recognition that idol worship is error; the following night scene continues the account. The present-form verb narrates a past event.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أنا أرينا إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض فبعثه ذلك أن حاج أباه وقومه في أمر الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects readings that make the kingdom-vision an interruption or say it began only when Abraham first saw a star.
rows.anchor: فاسد لا ينبغي أن يصار إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malakūt is an intensive form of mulk, analogous in formation to ṭāghūt and jabarūt; the Qur’an retains the word’s basic lexical meaning.
rows.anchor: فالملكوت هو الملك مصدر كالطاغوت والجبروت وإن كان آكد من حيث المعنى بالنسبة إلى الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human political ownership is a conventional social construct created for order, security, justice, and collective power, and can be transferred, gifted, seized, or usurped.
rows.anchor: إنما هو فيما عندنا معنى افتراضي اعتباري بعثنا إلى اعتباره الحاجة الاجتماعية إلى نظم الأعمال والأفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person’s command of hearing, sight, and actions operates by that person’s will, while these abilities depend on the person’s existence; the analogy prepares for God’s encompassing rule.
rows.anchor: فالإنسان يملك قوى نفسه وأفعال نفسه وهي جميعا تبعات وجوده قائمة به غير مستقلة عنه ولا مستغنية عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verses tie divine ownership of the kingdom to creation, grounding God’s sovereignty in the fact that all things derive their existence from Him.
rows.anchor: والآيات - كما ترى - تعلل الملك بالخلق فكون وجود الأشياء منه وانتساب الأشياء بوجودها وواقعيتها إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God creates all things, His ownership cannot be shared, transferred, or delegated so as to make Him unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وهو بمعنى ملكه الذي لا يشاركه فيه غيره ولا يزول عنه إلى غيره ولا يقبل نقلا ولا تفويضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command be and its creative effect show that the malakūt of each thing is its existence as dependent on God, a relation that admits no partner.
rows.anchor: فالآية الثانية تبين أن ملكوت كل شيء هو كلمة كن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lordship as ownership and governance cannot be delegated or transferred; contemplating creation’s malakūt therefore guides decisively to monotheism.
rows.anchor: فالربوبية التي هي الملك والتدبير لا تقبل تفويضا ولا تمليكا انتقاليا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s showing Abraham the malakūt meant that he saw things as dependent on their Creator; he then judged idols and changing heavenly bodies unfit to create or govern.
rows.anchor: توجيهه تعالى نفسه الشريفة إلى مشاهدة الأشياء من جهة استناد وجودها إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose lām in so that he be among the certain coordinates with an omitted clause; certainty means knowledge untouched by doubt, perhaps certainty about God’s signs and names.
rows.anchor: اللام للتعليل، والجملة معطوفة على أخرى محذوفة والتقدير ليكون كذا وكذا وليكون من الموقنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s certainty concerns God’s signs and leads to certainty about the divine names and attributes, as in the Qur’an’s description of leaders guided by God’s command.
rows.anchor: وينتج ذلك اليقين بأسماء الله الحسنى وصفاته العليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an does not make God’s essence an object of doubt or full human knowledge; the proper response is submission.
rows.anchor: وأما اليقين بذاته المتعالية فالقرآن يجله تعالى ان يتعلق به شك أو يحيط به علم وإنما يسلمه تسليما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an associates certain knowledge of its signs with disclosure of realities beyond sensory perception, including Hell and the record of the righteous witnessed by the near ones.
rows.anchor: من خواص العلم اليقيني بآياته تعالى إنكشاف ما وراء ستر الحس من حقائق الكون

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says the root j-n-n concerns hiding something from the senses; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī explains that night covering Abraham means darkness settling, not merely sunset.
rows.anchor: أصل الجن بفتح الجيم ستر الشيء عن الحاسة يقال جنه الليل وأجنه وجن عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night-and-star scene follows from Abraham’s rejection of idols and his prior vision of the kingdom: after God showed him creation’s dependence, night came and he saw a star.
rows.anchor: نريه الملكوت من الأشياء فأبطل ألوهية الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite a star avoids identifying a particular celestial body because Abraham’s argument applies to any setting star; the wording does not support an arbitrary pointed star among countless stars.
rows.anchor: فلا غرض في الكلام يتعلق بتعيين هذا الكوكب وأنه أي كوكب كان من السيارات أو الثوابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s people and the Sabians revered planets rather than fixed stars; since the moon and sun follow and Mercury is rarely visible, the star was probably Venus, Mars, Jupiter, or Saturn.
rows.anchor: والصابئون ما كانوا يعبدون أي كوكب ولا يحترمون إلا السيارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Venus is the likeliest star: it alone regularly follows the sun at dusk and can set before the moon rises; it is also the brightest planet and the first to catch the eye after darkness falls.
rows.anchor: على أن الزهرة أجمل الكواكب الدرية وأبهجها وأضوءها أول ما يجلب نظر الناظر إلى السماء

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
rows.claim: Some reports from the Imams of the Prophet’s household identify Abraham’s star as Venus; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this supports the astronomical inference.
rows.anchor: بعض الروايات عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أن الكوكب كان هو الزهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reconstruction, Venus appeared in the western sky after sunset during the latter lunar half, set an hour or two later, and the moon rose shortly afterward.
rows.anchor: فرأى الزهرة في الأفق الغربي حتى أفلت فرأى القمر بازغا بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here rabb means the owner or manager who governs affairs, not the Creator of heaven and earth, who is incorporeal, uncontained by place, and not an object of pointing.
rows.anchor: مالك الأشياء المربوبين، المدبر لأمرهم لا الذي فطر السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham already knew God; polytheists and Sabians generally assigned created subordinate beings delegated control over particular domains, so this is my lord identifies a proposed governor, not a creator equal to God.
rows.anchor: أراد به إثبات أنه رب يدبر الأمر لا إله فاطر مبدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s final declaration of devotion to the Creator shows that he was proving no partner exists, not proving that God exists; he already accepted one creator while asking who governs created affairs.
rows.anchor: فإن ظاهره أنه ينصرف عن فرض الشريك إلى إثبات أن لا شريك له لا أنه يثبت وجوده تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tests whether star, moon, or sun could administer affairs that belong either to God or to a creature delegated authority; their changing states make each candidate doubtful.
rows.anchor: وإنما يبحث عن أن هذا الرب المدبر للأمر أهو الله سبحانه وإليه يرجع التدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If read as real hypotheses, Abraham’s statements describe the required transition from immature ignorance to rationally seeking belief, before full knowledge and religious accountability; testing alternatives by observed signs is proper inquiry.
rows.anchor: فزمن حياته منقسم لا محالة إلى قسمين هما قبل التمييز والبلوغ وبعد التمييز والبلوغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus and John are exceptional cases who displayed understanding before the usual age of discernment; their miraculous maturity is not the ordinary human course.
rows.anchor: كما يحكيه القرآن عن المسيح ويحيى عليهما السلام فإنما ذلك من خوارق العادة الجارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before completing the reasoning, Abraham’s statements about the heavenly bodies are hypotheses for testing, not settled beliefs or shirk; the verses depict him waiting for the result.
rows.anchor: فهو ما لم يتم له الاستدلال غير قاطع بشيء ولا بان على شيء وإنما هو مفترض ومقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of his dialogue with Azar supports that Abraham already knew God and used this is my lord as rhetorical accommodation, adopting the opponents’ assumption to expose its failure.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فقوله { هذا ربي } جار مجرى التسليم والمجاراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afūl means setting; a setting star cannot govern continuously, while real lordship entails a lasting relation that draws the dependent creature to love its Lord.
rows.anchor: وفيه إبطال ربوبية الكوكب بعروض صفة الأفول له فإن الكوكب الغارب ينقطع بغروبه ممن طلع عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A true Lord must be permanent and unchanging; people attach themselves to transient beauty only when desire distracts them from its passing away.
rows.anchor: فمن الواجب أن يكون الرب ثابت الوجود غير متغير الأحوال كهذه الزخارف المزوقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī insists that the setting-star reasoning is a demonstrative argument, even if it might look like rhetoric or poetry.
rows.anchor: وهذا وجه برهاني وإن كان ربما يتخيل أنه بيان خطابي أو شعري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī cites a report from al-Ṣādiq asking whether religion is anything but love, in support of the connection between worship and love.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في المروي عن الصادق عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct proof is that lordship entails being loved, while what lacks enduring beauty cannot command natural love and therefore cannot be Lord.
rows.anchor: لأن الربوبية والألوهية تلازمان المحبوبية فما لا يتعلق به الحب الغريزي الفطري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers the direct argument: lordship entails being loved, while what lacks enduring beauty cannot command natural love and therefore cannot be Lord.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه هو الظاهر يتكئ عليه سياق الاحتجاج في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common predicate setting applies to star, moon, and sun, so Abraham repeats the proof; he may not yet have known moon and sun also set, or may be addressing different audiences.
rows.anchor: وذلك إما لكونه عليه السلام لم يكن مسبوق الذهن من أمر القمر والشمس وأنهما يطلعان ويغربان كالكوكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By using the language of rational beings for what he does not love, Abraham suggests that objects without awareness or reason cannot merit lordship, as in his questions about idols’ hearing, benefit, and harm.
rows.anchor: وكأنه للإشارة إلى أن غير أولي الشعور والعقل لا يستحق الربوبية من رأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon’s this is my lord repeats the earlier hypothetical or accommodating argument; after it sets, the conditional plea for guidance implies persistence would have made Abraham one of the deluded moon-worshippers.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الوضع الذي ذكره في القمر بقوله { هذا ربي } كان ضلالا لو دام وأصر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage implies there were people who assigned lordship to the moon and, after the sun episode, to the sun as well.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام إشارة أولا إلى أنه كان هناك قوم قائلون بربوبية القمر كالكوكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether Abraham was truly testing possibilities or accommodating his audience, he was seeking divine guidance and certain judgment; he already knew a Lord governed his affairs and wondered whether that Lord was the Creator or a created delegate.
rows.anchor: وثانيا أنه عليه السلام كان وقتئذ في مسير الطلب راجيا للهداية الإلهية مترقبا لما يفيض ربه عليه من النظر الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having repeated this is my lord for the moon, Abraham adds the sun is greater as an excuse for again positing its lordship after his preceding hypothesis failed.
rows.anchor: ليكون بمنزلة الاعتذار للعود إلى فرض الربوبية لها مع تبين خطاء افتراضه مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine demonstrative this may suggest Abraham did not yet identify the luminous body’s type; he may have first seen star, moon, and sun emerging from concealment as bright objects.
rows.anchor: الإتيان في الإشارة بلفظ المذكر هو الذي يستريح إليه من لا يميز المشار إليه في نوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence suggests Abraham stayed with the star hypothesis until he saw it set; had he known it would set, he could have refuted its lordship as directly as he refuted idols.
rows.anchor: فإن فيه إشعارا بأنه عليه السلام مكث بانيا على كون الكوكب ربا حتى شاهد غروبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain masculine this by supplying an understood masculine noun such as object or luminous body; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the usage is valid but rejects it without a reason that licenses the shift.
rows.anchor: منهم من قال تذكير الإشارة إنما هو بتأويل المشار إليه أو الجرم النير السماوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the demonstrative agrees with the masculine predicates lord and greater; he rejects this because Abraham’s people recognized female deities, and greater is an invariant comparative form rather than proof of masculine agreement.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال إنه من قبيل إتباع المبتدء للخبر في تذكيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some claim the masculine form honors the sun and protects divinity from femininity; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī counters that Babylonians themselves worshipped many goddesses.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال إن تذكير الإشارة إنما هو لتعظيم الشمس حيث نسب إليها الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arab polytheists called their idols female and called an idol a tribe’s daughter; a report on 4:117 explains that they named their gods as females.
rows.anchor: أنهم كانوا يسمون آلهتهم إناثا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Abraham’s people considered the sun male and assigned it a wife named Anunit; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī replies that this belief cannot change the feminine grammar for sun.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال إن قوم إبراهيم عليه السلام كانوا يعدون الشمس من الذكور وقد أثبتوا لها زوجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposal that Abraham spoke ungendered Syriac is rejected: grammatical forms depend on the language, and other Qur’anic quotations of Abraham preserve feminine agreement for the sun.
rows.anchor: على أنه تعالى حكى عن إبراهيم عليه السلام احتجاجات كثيرة وأدعية وافرة في القرآن وفيها موارد كثيرة اعتبر فيها التأنيث

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One interpreter argues that Abraham, Ishmael, and Hagar spoke ancient Arabic, citing claims of Arab settlement in Chaldea and Egypt, an Arab Hammurabi, and Abraham’s later ties to Mecca and Jurhum.
rows.anchor: ومن عجيب ما أورد على هذا الوجه ما ذكره بعض المفسرين وأصر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The placement of the kingdom-vision and certainty among Abraham’s arguments shows that his reasoning came from witnessed realities of creation and rested on certainty, especially his rejection of setting stars.
rows.anchor: يدل على أنه عليه السلام إنما كان يأخذ ما يلقيه من الحجة على أبيه وقومه مما كان يشاهده من ملكوت السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some commentators reduce I do not love those that set to a popular insinuation that the ignorant worshippers’ stars become hidden from them and do not know their worshippers’ affairs.
rows.anchor: إذ يقول والصواب أن الكلام كان تعريضا خفيا لا برهانا نظريا جليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the popular-argument reading: the surrounding certainty and malakūt passages show the proof is demonstrative, and it rests on love and its absence, not on setting alone.
rows.anchor: وخفي عليه ثانيا أن الحجة بنيت على الحب وعدمه لا على الأفول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an likens worldly life to vegetation suddenly cut down after flourishing, illustrating why transience should weaken attachment to worldly pleasures.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازينت وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an contrasts what perishes with what endures, teaching that what is with God is better and lasting.
rows.anchor: ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: I do not love those that set means beings who disappear and do not endure cannot command human love; since the worshipped Lord must be loved, setting celestial bodies cannot be lords.
rows.anchor: أن الذي من شأنه أن يفقده الإنسان ويغيب عنه ولا يبقى ولا يثبت له لا يستحق أن يحبه الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the opposing commentator confuses rising with a trait of lordship; the verse does not build its proof on rising, so that reading leaves the question unanswered.
rows.anchor: هو البزوغ وهو الطلوع والظهور بعد خفاء المنافي للربوبية

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf says setting makes the argument clearer than rising because it involves concealment; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī answers that only setting frustrates the love required by lordship, whereas rising does not.
rows.anchor: الاحتجاج بالأفول أظهر لأنه انتقال مع خفاء واحتجاب
